characteristics.name: Methods

characteristics.value:

references.title: The effectiveness of daily SMS reminders in pharmaceutical care of older adults on improving patients' adherence to antihypertensive medication (SPPA): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Parallel group, randomised trial

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Inclusion criteria:

  • "Age ≥ 55 years (from the day of the 55th birthday inclusive)"
  • "Diagnosis of primary hypertension (I10 according to ICD-10)"
  • "Filling of antihypertensive prescription(s) at trial recruitment (Visit 1)"
  • "Duration of antihypertensive drug treatment for at least one year without any discontinuation"
  • "Ownership of a mobile phone for personal use with the ability to open and read SMS"
  • "Understanding of Slovak language on native-speaker level"
  • "Informed consent for participation in the clinical trial and personally signed informed consent form"

Exclusion criteria:

"Exclusion criteria assessed prior to patient enrolment (by trial pharmacists)":

  • "Planned hospitalisation during the trial period (3 months)"
  • "Biological impairment affecting the ability to read the SMS (e.g. loss of vision, visual field cuts, aphasia)"
  • "Living in the same household with another trial participant"
  • "Participation in another clinical trial"

"Exclusion criteria assessed after patient enrolment (by trial pharmacists and project leader)":

  • "Hospitalisation during the trial period"
  • "Patient informs he/she won't be able to participate in the trial"
  • "Withdrawal of Informed Consent"

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value: "Participants in the intervention group will receive sPhC provided by the trial pharmacist, the welcome SMS, and the end-of-trial SMS. Additionally, they will be receiving the investigated intervention, daily SMS reminders of antihypertensive medication intake, for three months."

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome: 

  • "Combined adherence endpoint"

Secondary outcomes:

  • "Change in medians of MMAS-8"
  • "Mean Adherence Rate (%) calculated via pill count"
  • "Mean change in systolic BP"
  • "Patients' satisfaction with SMS reminders."

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value: Identified from a trial registry record and a published protocol with a completed status. No study results are posted in the registry. Due to insufficient information, this study was currently classified as awaiting classification.

references.authors: Park JE, Lee JE, Moon BK, Lee H, Park SH, Kim SK, et al
references.title: Impact of a pharmaceutical care service for patients with rheumatoid arthritis using a customised mobile device (the PROUD trial): study protocol for a randomised controlled trial

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Parallel group, randomised trial

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Inclusion criteria:

  • "Be at least 18 years old"
  • "Be diagnosed with RA by a rheumatologist at the DCMC and prescribed at least one of the following DMARDs: conventional synthetic DMARDs (hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, sulfasalazine, bucillamine or leflunomide), biological DMARDs administered subcutaneously (etanercept, adalimumab, golimumab, abatacept or tocilizumab) and JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, baricitinib or upadacitinib)"
  • "Taking DMARDs, steroids or analgesics for the first time for the management of RA or changed prescription of DMARDs at the time of randomisation"
  • "Using a mobile device such as a smartphone"

Exclusion criteria:

  • "Are unable to respond to surveys or interviews due to deterioration in cognitive abilities or other similar conditions"
  • "Have severe systemic or malignant diseases"
  • "Fail or disagree to install a mobile application called MediRA which is a customised medication guide for patients with RA"
  • "Are deemed inappropriate to provide regular telepharmacy service using telecommunications due to hearing impairment"

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value: "The participants randomised to the TC group will receive the ICT-integrated pharmaceutical care service by the clinical pharmacists at the DCMC in addition to the existing pharmacist services at community pharmacies. For the participants in the TC group, the clinical pharmacists will review the laboratory results, medication and disease history of the participants in the electronic medical records (EMRs), and the participants will be called every month for medication counselling."

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome: 

  • "The changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL)"

  • "Changes in validated Korean version of the Pharmacy Service Questionnaire (K-PSQ) scores"
  • "Changes in clinical parameters such as erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) level, C reactive protein (CRP) level, pain score as measured by a 0–10 Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), and number of joint involvements"
  • "Frequency of acute care utilisation"

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value: The trial registry record could not be accessed at the time of this review, and the recruitment status could not be confirmed. No results were identified. This study was currently classified as awaiting classification.

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Parallel group, randomised trial

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Inclusion criteria:

  • "Diagnosed with valvular heart disease, who underwent valve surgery at the hospital received warfarin education from clinical pharmacists before discharge"
  • "If they had been on warfarin treatment for at least 3 months"
  • "Received warfarin management through either the Alfalfa app or pharmacist-led outpatient clinic visits"
  • "Agreed to regular follow-up"
  • "Had no serious bleeding or thrombotic events in the 3 months before warfarin treatment"

Exclusion criteria:

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value: Participants received anticoagulation management through a pharmacist-led mobile application (Alfalfa app). The application also enabled communication between patients and pharmacists for ongoing management.

references.title: An asthma self-management program based on WeChat to improve asthma control and quality of life: a randomized controlled trial
The influence and effect evaluation of pharmacist participation on self-management of patients with asthma

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Parallel group, randomised trial

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Inclusion criteria:

  • "Age ≥ 18 years"
  • "Ability to complete questionnaires independently"
  • "Willingness to participate in a self-management intervention"
  • "Confirmed diagnosis of moderate to severe asthma"
  • "Receipt of standard treatment for at least 6 months"
  • "Use of a smartphone with WeChat"

Exclusion criteria:

  • "Pregnant or lactating women"
  • "With serious cardiovascular, hepatic, renal and mental disorders"
  • "Who were attending other self-management program"
  • "Whose asthma control test score was complete control"
  • "Acute severe attacks require hospitalization"
  • "Were unable to communicate"

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value: Participants received a WeChat-based self-management programme in addition to usual care. The programme included symptom monitoring through daily asthma diaries and regular assessment using the Asthma Control Test, educational materials, automated reminders, and communication with pharmacists via the application. Pharmacists monitored patient-reported data and provided feedback or interventions as needed. Participants were also required to upload inhaler technique videos for evaluation until competency was achieved.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome: 

  • "Asthma control"

Secondary outcomes:

  • "Pulmonary function (FEV1% predicted)"
  • "Asthma Self-Management Behaviour Questionnaire (ASMQ)"
  • "Asthma Quality of Life Questionnaire (AQLQ)"
  • "Healthcare utilisation (emergency department visits and hospitalisations)"

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value: This study was initially identified based on registry information (ChiCTR2300075425). A full-text publication (Xu S 2025) was subsequently identified through handsearching; however, the study has not yet been assessed for inclusion and will be considered in a future update of the review. The study therefore remains classified as awaiting classification.
